name: Deadmire
summary: In Dustwallow Marsh, hunters seek Deadmire in the waterways north of the Stonemaul Ruins. Melor Stonehoof asks you to bring back a tooth from the ancient crocolisk. The hunt teaches tracking and mercy.

sections.title: A Hunt of Mercy
sections.body: From Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, Melor Stonehoof sends you east to Dustwallow Marsh. He teaches promising trackers the spiritual traditions of the hunt. Tauren hunters seek reverence and a bond with the natural world, not slaughter or trophies. There, you are to find Deadmire, an ancient crocolisk whose long life has become a burden.

sections.title: The Ancient of the Marsh
sections.body: North of the Stonemaul Ruins, Deadmire prowls the waterways as a massive, pale crocolisk. His strength and fury still flare in sudden bursts, but age has worn down his body. Grinding bones bring unrelenting pain. Melor asks you to grant him a swift, honorable end and bring back one tooth as a token of his release.

faq.answer: Deadmire is a massive, ancient white crocolisk in the swamps of Dustwallow Marsh. He remains dangerous, though his aged body is failing and brings him pain.

faq.q: Why does Melor Stonehoof want Deadmire killed?
faq.answer: Melor Stonehoof asks you to kill Deadmire as an act of mercy. The crocolisk's aging bones cause him maddening pain, and Melor believes releasing his spirit is a sacred duty.
Deadmire prowls the waterways north of the Stonemaul Ruins in Dustwallow Marsh.

faq.q: What proof does Melor require from the hunt?
faq.answer: Melor asks you to bring back one of Deadmire's teeth as proof of the hunt.

faq.q: What does this hunt teach aspiring hunters?
faq.answer: The hunt teaches you that a hunter's calling means more than killing. It means honoring nature and recognizing when a creature's life has become suffering.
Melor Stonehoof, a tauren hunter, offers the hunt on Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff.

angles.text: As a hunter, you balance skill in the hunt with spiritual responsibility. An honorable kill can be an act of mercy.
As a tauren, you honor the Earth Mother's creatures and respect the natural cycles of life and death.
As a Horde traveler, you take part in hunts for Thunder Bluff's elders and learn the land and traditions of your tauren allies.
